repo_state_at_start: main @ 253ab39 (PR #50 merged). 71 rows across Datasets A (19), B (31) and C (9 SOL + 12 BND); 14 seller records; verification log at 185 checks across passes P1-P11.
method: Live re-fetch of the gold spot page, then a rotating sample chosen for price volatility and for the values the melt calculator consumes: R20 (the only Sarraf row carrying both a price and a weight), all three Menē 24k bands (Menē re-quotes with the metal, and every one of its rows had already moved once today), BND-04 (a published 1.7 g weight) and R03 (a price corrected in an earlier pass). Each stored value was searched for verbatim in the returned page text; nothing was inferred from a collection grid, a related-products widget or a search snippet.
no_hallucination_rule: A value is only recorded if the cited page prints it. A number that cannot be re-read is left exactly as captured and flagged, never replaced by a nearby figure.

checks.label: GoldPrice.org spot page re-read live
checks.findings: The live page printed 'Spot Gold Price: USD 3,997.22 / Ounce | Spot Silver Price: USD 53.92 / Ounce' with the label 'Oct 23rd, 2026 at 04:17 NY Time'; the page-header ticker read '3,996.89 / -47.83 / -1.18%'. The stored primary snapshot in data/prices.json is USD 4,022.22 / oz labelled 'Oct 23rd, 2026 at 05:55 NY Time'. The live reading is 0.62% lower than the stored capture on the same market date, and the page's own clock label (04:17 NY) is EARLIER than the 05:55 NY label on the stored capture even though it was read later in the day. Both facts are recorded and neither is explained away: the stored snapshot is left untouched so every melt figure on the site keeps reproducing the arithmetic it documents, and the timestamp inversion is raised as an irregularity for review.
checks.action: No data change to prices.json. Live reading recorded here, in data/reverification-57724486.json and in finding F39. Flag PRC1 refreshed.
